questions.q: What is Microsoft Defender for Cloud's signature output that summarizes an environment's posture?
questions.explain: Defender for Cloud reports a Secure Score, a percentage summarizing alignment with the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark.

questions.q: Can Microsoft Defender for Cloud assess resources outside of Azure?
options: Yes -- it can also connect to and assess AWS and GCP accounts
No, it works only with Azure resources
questions.explain: Despite its name, Defender for Cloud is a multicloud posture tool that can also assess AWS and GCP accounts from the same dashboard.

questions.q: What is the primary role of AWS Security Hub?
options: Aggregating findings from AWS's own security services and third-party tools into one view
questions.explain: Security Hub is primarily an aggregator, consolidating findings from existing services rather than replacing them.

questions.q: Which of these is a real AWS service whose findings Security Hub aggregates?
questions.explain: Security Hub pulls findings from AWS's own services including GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and IAM Access Analyzer.

questions.q: What do both Defender for Cloud and Security Hub ultimately produce from their checks?
options: A score reflecting alignment with a recognized security benchmark
questions.explain: Both tools check findings against a recognized standard and compress the result into a score a team can track.
